name: Recording instrument general symbol
summary: General square form for an instrument that keeps a time record of a quantity rather than just displaying it.
description: A recording instrument keeps a record of a measured quantity over time, traditionally on a paper chart and now usually in memory. IEC-style diagrams draw it as a square, with the placeholder replaced by the recorded quantity, so it can be told apart from a simple indicating meter at a glance.

The square does not say how often samples are stored, how long records are retained or how they are retrieved. Those details are what make a recording useful in an investigation, and they belong in the instrument specification rather than on the symbol.
readingNotes: Identify what quantity is recorded and its source.
Check how records are retrieved or exported.
distinction: A recording instrument stores values against time; an indicating instrument shows only the present value.
